blocks.passage:
Project management is, at its heart, a promise to the business: "This will be ready, at this cost, with this quality, by this date." Every element of the discipline — planning, tracking, risk management, communication — is about protecting that promise.

Most projects do not fail because of technical issues. They fail because scope creeps quietly, risks are tracked but not managed, and stakeholders discover bad news too late. Good project managers make the invisible visible: they surface issues early, escalate without drama, and keep the business honestly informed about the state of the promise.

By the end of the month, a skilled PM will already have adjusted the plan twice, flagged one risk to the sponsor, and rewritten the status update in plain English. By the end of the quarter, they will have kept the promise — or renegotiated it in time.

items.q: How does the text describe project management "at its heart"?
options: A promise about scope, cost, quality and date
items.why: "a promise to the business: 'This will be ready, at this cost, with this quality, by this date.'"

items.q: According to the text, why do most projects fail?
options: Scope creep, unmanaged risks and late bad news
items.why: "scope creeps quietly, risks are tracked but not managed, and stakeholders discover bad news too late."

items.q: What does "make the invisible visible" mean here?
options: Surface issues early and keep the business informed
items.why: "they surface issues early, escalate without drama, and keep the business honestly informed."

items.q: By the end of the quarter, a skilled PM will have…
options: kept the promise — or renegotiated it in time
items.why: "they will have kept the promise — or renegotiated it in time."

items.q: The phrase "escalate without drama" suggests a PM should raise issues…
items.why: Inferência: escalar sem drama é comunicar o problema de forma calma e objetiva.

audio.text:
Quick project update. We've got a milestone slipping, and I want to be straight with you about it rather than surprise you later.

The design phase is running about a week behind. By Friday we'll have finished the review, but the build was supposed to start Monday, and now it can't. That's the milestone at risk.

Here's the thing: the delay isn't really the design team's fault. The scope quietly grew — two extra features got added three weeks ago without moving the date. That's classic scope creep, and it's on me for not flagging it sooner.

So I've got two options for you, the sponsor. Option one: we hold the date and drop the two new features to a later release. Option two: we keep the features and move the launch two weeks. I'm leaning towards option one, but it's your call.

Whatever we choose, by the end of next week I'll have updated the plan and the risk register, and I'll keep the status update in plain English so everyone knows exactly where we stand.

items.q: Why is Oliver giving the update now rather than later?
options: To be straight about the slipping milestone rather than surprise the sponsor
items.why: "I want to be straight with you about it rather than surprise you later."

items.q: What caused the delay, according to Oliver?
options: Scope crept — two extra features were added without moving the date
items.why: "The scope quietly grew — two extra features got added three weeks ago without moving the date."

items.q: Who does Oliver say the scope creep is "on"?
options: Himself, for not flagging it sooner
items.why: "it's on me for not flagging it sooner."

items.q: What is option one?
options: Hold the date and drop the two new features to a later release
items.why: "Option one: we hold the date and drop the two new features to a later release."

items.q: What will Oliver have done by the end of next week?
options: Updated the plan and the risk register
items.why: "by the end of next week I'll have updated the plan and the risk register."

items.q: "We've got **scope creep** again." Scope creep is…
options: the work quietly expanding beyond the plan
items.why: Scope creep = expansão silenciosa do escopo.

items.q: A **milestone** in a project is…
items.why: Milestone = marco importante do projeto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Let's log that in the **risk ___** so the sponsor can see it."
items.why: Risk register = registro de riscos.

items.q: A **stakeholder** is…
options: anyone with an interest in the project's outcome
items.why: Stakeholder = parte interessada.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "This issue is serious — I'll ___ it to the sponsor today."
items.why: To escalate = escalar, levar a uma instância superior.

items.q: "The build is **behind schedule**." Behind schedule means…
items.why: Behind schedule = atrasado em relação ao plano.

items.q: "Let's **flag** this risk to the sponsor." To flag means to…
items.why: To flag = sinalizar, chamar atenção.

items.q: "We need to **keep track of** the dependencies." To keep track of means to…
items.why: Keep track of = acompanhar, monitorar.

items.q: "That feature can **wait for** the next release." To wait for means to…
items.why: Aqui, empurrar para (esperar até) o próximo release.

items.q: "Let's not **bite off more than we can chew** this sprint." This idiom means to…
options: take on more than we can handle
items.why: Bite off more than you can chew = assumir mais do que se dá conta.
